one-runner-per-tick.name: One runner per tick
one-runner-per-tick.statement: N copies of a scheduler share one schedule, so something must pick exactly one runner per tick.

dead-holder-blocks-forever.name: A dead holder blocks forever
dead-holder-blocks-forever.statement: A lock with no expiry outlives a crashed holder and blocks everyone, forever.

lock-ttl.name: TTL sets recovery time
lock-ttl.statement: A TTL bounds how long a dead holder can block; it is the crash-recovery time.

lease-renewal.name: Lease renewal
lease-renewal.statement: A long job keeps a short TTL by renewing while alive; renewing at TTL/2 leaves one retry of margin before expiry.

ttl-vs-renewal-interval.name: TTL and renewal interval are separate knobs
ttl-vs-renewal-interval.statement: TTL sets recovery time; the renewal interval trades safety margin against coordination overhead.

ownership-token.name: Ownership token
ownership-token.statement: Renew or release only if the stored token is yours, so an expired holder can't free the next holder's lock.

zombie-release-cascade.name: Zombie release cascade
zombie-release-cascade.statement: An expired holder that still releases frees a live holder's lock, letting more runners pile on.

lock-guards-holders-not-execution.name: A lock guards holders, not execution
lock-guards-holders-not-execution.statement: Deleting a lock key doesn't stop code already running; correctness needs idempotency or fencing, not the lock.

registry-over-switch.name: Registry over switch
registry-over-switch.statement: A per-type registry keeps each type's logic together where a giant switch scatters it.

mapped-type-exhaustiveness.name: Mapped-type exhaustiveness
mapped-type-exhaustiveness.statement: A mapped type over the type union makes a missing registry entry a compile error.

callback-injection-breaks-cycle.name: Injection breaks an import cycle
callback-injection-breaks-cycle.statement: Receiving a function as an argument instead of importing it breaks a circular import.

orphaned-position-record.name: Orphaned position record
orphaned-position-record.statement: Deleting a node leaves contacts' position records pointing at nothing.

forwarding-redirect.name: Forwarding redirect
forwarding-redirect.statement: On delete, leave a redirect from the old node id to a live target.

redirect-chains.name: Redirects chain
redirect-chains.statement: Redirects stack (x→y→z), so resolving a position means following hops.

backward-enumeration.name: Enumerate backward
backward-enumeration.statement: To find contacts affected by deleting Z, enumerate every source whose chain ends at Z, not just records equal to Z.

cascading-delete-set.name: Cascading delete set
cascading-delete-set.statement: A delete can take dependents with it (experiment → variants); affected-contact logic must compose over the whole set.

caller-owned-transaction.name: The caller owns the transaction
caller-owned-transaction.statement: A helper that writes related records takes the caller's tx and never opens its own, so all commit or none do.

throw-rolls-back.name: Throwing is what rolls back
throw-rolls-back.statement: Throwing inside a transaction triggers rollback; returning an error result lets the partial writes commit.

throw-vs-return.name: Throw vs return
throw-vs-return.statement: Expected, user-caused failures return a result; invariant violations and mid-transaction failures throw.

registry-as-decoupling.name: A partial registry as decoupling
registry-as-decoupling.statement: A deliberately partial registry can keep the pure graph model from importing the database layer.

lost-update.name: Lost update
lost-update.statement: Two read-modify-write saves of a whole document race; the second silently clobbers the first.

optimistic-concurrency.name: Optimistic concurrency
optimistic-concurrency.statement: Save only if the version is still the one you read (compare-and-swap); detect the collision at write time instead of locking.

claim-revision-up-front.name: Claim the revision up front
claim-revision-up-front.statement: Claiming the revision first fails fast and takes the row lock, so a concurrent edit blocks, then fails.

redirect-map-keeps-tx-short.name: One map entry keeps the edit short
redirect-map-keeps-tx-short.statement: A delete writes one O(1) redirect entry so the edit transaction stays short; the O(N) bookmark rewrite moves to an async job.

redirect-resolution-walk.name: The resolution walk
redirect-resolution-walk.statement: Resolve by hopping until a live node (success), a repeat (cycle), or nothing (dead end).

load-bearing-waypoint.name: Load-bearing waypoint
load-bearing-waypoint.statement: A middle redirect with no contacts of its own still carries chains through it; cleanup must keep whole chains.

priority-cant-reclaim.name: Priority can't reclaim committed capacity
priority-cant-reclaim.statement: Reactive priority has a ceiling; protecting a class means holding slack in advance.

aimd-asymmetry.name: AIMD asymmetry
aimd-asymmetry.statement: Increase gently, cut sharply; the asymmetry keeps a controller out of the danger zone.

wait-time-signal.name: Control on wait time
wait-time-signal.statement: Steer on wait time against the SLA (end-user impact), not queue length.

atomic-check-and-spend.name: Atomic check-and-spend
atomic-check-and-spend.statement: Checking and spending a shared budget must be one atomic operation, or two spenders both see the last dollar.

bounded-turn-round-robin.name: Bounded-turn round robin
bounded-turn-round-robin.statement: Round robin with bounded turns bounds a tenant's wait by tenant count, not by backlog.

claim-lease-sweep.name: Claim, lease, sweep
claim-lease-sweep.statement: Claiming moves work to an in-progress set stamped with an expiry; a sweeper requeues expired claims.

orthogonal-throttles.name: Two orthogonal throttles
orthogonal-throttles.statement: Class priority (token bucket) and tenant fairness (leases) are independent axes.

common-case-top-level.name: Common case at the top level
common-case-top-level.statement: Make the common case the top-level shape and put variation in optional additive fields, so growth never reshapes the contract.

per-resource-addressing.name: Address each sub-resource
per-resource-addressing.statement: Making each sub-thing its own resource keeps every response a single object; the cost is N+1 fan-out.

counts-not-rates.name: Ship counts, not rates
counts-not-rates.statement: A raw metrics API ships counts; a rate encodes a denominator choice the caller should make.

serve-vs-maintain.name: Expensive to serve vs to maintain
serve-vs-maintain.statement: Costly to keep fresh is not costly to serve: a maintained cache serves instantly.

cache-shared-not-unique.name: Cache what's shared
cache-shared-not-unique.statement: Cache what many requests share; per-request-unique work (arbitrary filters) is what stays expensive to serve.

generator-call-runs-nothing.name: Calling a generator runs nothing
generator-call-runs-nothing.statement: Calling a generator function runs none of its body; the first pull starts it, so a query inside fires on first pull.

yield-freezes-the-frame.name: Yield freezes the frame
yield-freezes-the-frame.statement: A yield mid-loop parks the whole frame, so the row in hand survives to the next pull.

generator-pipeline-stages.name: Stages compose
generator-pipeline-stages.statement: Each stage takes an async iterable and returns one, so stages chain into a pipeline.

fold-needs-grouped-input.name: A fold needs grouped input
fold-needs-grouped-input.statement: A streaming fold assumes rows arrive grouped by key; unsorted input yields several transitions per key.

silent-wrongness-misattribution.name: Silent wrongness misdirects debugging
silent-wrongness-misattribution.statement: A silently wrong result sends you debugging the wrong layer.

editor-ships-buffer.name: The editor ships the buffer
editor-ships-buffer.statement: The editor owns the unsaved buffer, so it must send its contents to the server (didOpen / didChange).

requests-point-at-positions.name: Requests point at positions
requests-point-at-positions.statement: A hover or completion names a position; the server already holds the text.

line-column-edit-locality.name: Line + column survive edits
line-column-edit-locality.statement: Line/column addresses stay valid when text changes elsewhere; flat offsets shift for everything after an edit.

one-checker-two-doors.name: One checker, two doors
one-checker-two-doors.statement: Batch tsc and the language server run the same checker; LSP is a protocol door, not the brain.

translator-hop-cost.name: The translator hop was the cost
translator-hop-cost.statement: The old language server translated every keystroke's request; removing that hop is the speedup.

correlation-tag.name: Correlation tag
correlation-tag.statement: Stamp your own id onto the outgoing mail so SES echoes it back on every event.

durable-row-before-send.name: Durable row before send
durable-row-before-send.statement: The row a tag points to must exist before the send, or a crash leaves the tag pointing at nothing.

raw-ledger-replay.name: Raw ledger enables replay
raw-ledger-replay.statement: Keeping the raw events lets you fix a counting bug and recompute; counters alone are their own only copy.

readers-decoupled.name: Readers are decoupled
readers-decoupled.statement: Each reader of the ledger is its own program, so adding or removing one never touches ingest and one failing doesn't half-finish the others.

cursor-redelivery.name: Crash before bookmark re-reads
cursor-redelivery.statement: A reader that applies effects but dies before saving its bookmark re-reads the same events next tick.

counts-and-bookmark-atomic.name: Effects and bookmark move together
counts-and-bookmark-atomic.statement: Applying effects and moving the bookmark must commit in one transaction.

bookmark-lives-with-effects.name: Bookmark lives with the effects
bookmark-lives-with-effects.statement: With no cross-database transaction, the bookmark lives in the database the reader writes to; reading twice is harmless.

commit-order-not-stamp-order.name: Commit order is not stamp order
commit-order-not-stamp-order.statement: Rows stamped when their insert begins can commit out of order, so a reader can skip past a slow insert forever.

safety-lag.name: Safety lag
safety-lag.statement: Readers only take rows older than now minus X, and X is bounded by the insert's timeout.

retention-slowest-reader.name: Keep from the slowest reader
retention-slowest-reader.statement: Cleanup keeps everything from the oldest reader bookmark onward.

frozen-bookmark-pins-retention.name: A frozen bookmark pins the ledger
frozen-bookmark-pins-retention.statement: A deleted reader's leftover bookmark pins the ledger forever.

no-bookmark-row-means-unborn.name: No row means not born yet
no-bookmark-row-means-unborn.statement: A reader has no bookmark row until its first tick, so a missing row means the reader hasn't run yet.

bookmark-name-contract.name: The bookmark name is a contract
bookmark-name-contract.statement: Retention looks readers up by exact name, so a future reader must write its bookmark under the pre-chosen name or the guard never engages.

sqs-in-flight-invisible.name: Received = hidden, not removed
sqs-in-flight-invisible.statement: ReceiveMessage hides a message for the visibility timeout; only DeleteMessage removes it, otherwise it becomes visible again when the timeout lapses.

sqs-at-least-once.name: SQS is at-least-once
sqs-at-least-once.statement: A consumer can finish the work and die (or time out) before DeleteMessage, so any message can be processed more than once; the queue cannot tell 'done but not deleted' from 'never done'.

throw-waits-out-visibility.name: A thrown job waits out its visibility
throw-waits-out-visibility.statement: A handler that throws (or returns {retry: true}) is not retried immediately: the message is simply not deleted, and it reappears only when its current visibility lapses — up to 30s after the last receive or extension.

crash-recovery-is-visibility.name: Crash recovery time = visibility timeout
crash-recovery-is-visibility.statement: When a worker dies mid-job its extension timer dies with it, so the message reappears at most one visibility timeout (30s) after the last receive or extension — the timeout, not the 20s extension interval, sets recovery time.

visibility-heartbeat.name: Visibility extension is lease renewal
visibility-heartbeat.statement: Loops calls ChangeMessageVisibility every 20s to push the deadline back to 30s from now, so a live handler of any length keeps its message with 10s of margin per beat; the timer is cleared before delete.

visibility-is-not-a-job-timeout.name: Visibility timeout is not a job timeout
visibility-is-not-a-job-timeout.statement: When visibility lapses nothing stops the running handler; the message is handed to a second consumer while the first is still working, so the two run concurrently.

receive-count-redrive.name: Receive count drives the DLQ
receive-count-redrive.statement: Every receive bumps a message's receive count; once it exceeds the redrive policy's maxReceiveCount (3 for loops queues) SQS moves it to dlq-<queue> instead of delivering it again — thrown and {retry: true} attempts both count.

timeout-doesnt-cancel-remote.name: Your timeout doesn't cancel their write
timeout-doesnt-cancel-remote.statement: Giving up on a request on your side (a Promise.race timeout) doesn't stop the server from committing it, so 'it threw' does not mean 'it didn't happen'.

idempotency-key-minted-before-retry-boun.name: Mint the idempotency key outside the retry loop
idempotency-key-minted-before-retry-boun.statement: A dedupe key only dedupes retries that reuse it, so it must be minted before the outermost retry boundary — at enqueue, carried in the message — not per call (svix mints a fresh key per message.create).

nested-retry-layers.name: Retry layers nest
nested-retry-layers.statement: svix's client retries (3 attempts, 50ms/100ms) run inside one SQS delivery, which retries every ~30s up to 3 receives; each layer dedupes only within the scope where its key was minted, and an inner timeout must fit the server's own idempotency lock.
